fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Pilate, the Roman governor, asks Jesus, "Are You the King of the Jews?" (Matthew 27:11). Jesus answers, "You have said so…" Pilate asks a yes or no question and gets a short answer back.

Not this one, friend. The question is about a king, not a priest. Pilate asks, "Are You the King of the Jews?" (Matthew 27:11). The chief priests and elders are the ones bringing accusations, but the title Pilate raises is King.

That's right. Jesus doesn't argue back. The text says that when He was accused by the chief priests and elders, "…He gave no answer." (Matthew 27:12). Picture accusations coming from the chief priests and elders, and Jesus giving no answer. I can't even stay quiet when the oven timer beeps.
Not that one, friend. The text doesn't have Pilate walking away. It says Jesus gave no answer, "…much to the governor’s amazement." (Matthew 27:14). Amazement is what the text gives us.
Not a soldier, friend. The custom was to release a prisoner, one the crowd chose (Matthew 27:15). The text says prisoner, and that's the word that fits.

Not a servant, friend. The text says the custom at the feast was to release "…a prisoner of their choosing." (Matthew 27:15). I read that verse twice looking for a servant and came up empty. The crowd gets to pick, and the word for who they're picking is prisoner.

You got it, baker. Pilate's wife sends this message: "Have nothing to do with that innocent man…" (Matthew 27:19). She calls Jesus innocent, and the message reaches Pilate while he is sitting on the judgment seat. Her words say it loud and clear.
Nobody's booking a trip to Galilee in this message, friend. She says, "Have nothing to do with that innocent man…" (Matthew 27:19). She calls Jesus innocent, and that's the heart of what she sends.

That's right, friend. Her message says, "…for I have suffered terribly in a dream today because of Him." (Matthew 27:19). The text doesn't tell us what the dream was. I think it shook her up. I'd be sending that message too.
Yes, friend. Pilate says, "I am innocent of this man’s blood…" (Matthew 27:24). He says it while washing his hands in front of the crowd. Innocent is the word he picks for himself.
